newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower, Dec falters at expiry.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower, Dec falters at expiry.

text.p: MGE spring wheat ended lower on perceptions it was overvalued at Wednesday's close relative to other markets, and nearby December expired sharply lower on a lack of interest, traders said.

Open interest in the December contract was 705,000 bushels heading into the final day of the contract's life. One trader said the expiry disappointed locals who had hoped that some parties waited until the last day to clear out of their longs in the Dec contract.
"There was a total lack of interest in the Dec," the trader said.
Spring wheat lagged other U.S. wheat markets throughout the session amid feelings that Minneapolis closed too high Wednesday relative to Kansas City and Chicago.
"This really isn't overhead resistance as much as it is an attempt to bring our values back in line with the other markets," an MGE floor source said at the midsession.
MGE spring wheat closed 1/2 to 14 cents per bushel lower, with Dec down 14 cents at $4.23. March lost 3-1/2 cents to close at $3.96-3/4.
Traders said CIS was the featured seller in the March and Con Agra sold the May.
MGE barley futures closed unchanged to three cents per cwt higher, with Dec expiring unchanged at $6.73.
